title: Hybrid GPU Programming Education with Python and C++: Preferences, Performance and Common Python Pitfalls
problem: GPU programming education faces language choice trade-offs; students prefer familiar languages but may face performance barriers; Python-specific pitfalls in GPU contexts are not well documented
motivation: GPU programming is increasingly important but entry barriers remain high. Offering multiple language options (Python vs C++) can improve accessibility, but trade-offs between learning outcomes and language choice are unclear.
method: The researchers taught 19 computer science students (both undergraduates and graduate students) GPU programming in two ways: using Python paired with Numba, a compiler that converts Python code to run on graphics processors, and using C++ with CUDA, the standard programming framework for GPUs. They checked what students knew beforehand, measured how each approach performed, and analyzed what specific mistakes students made in each language.
key_novelty: This study measured specific mistakes students make in Python GPU programming and their impact on learning outcomes compared to C++.
contributions: Hybrid GPU programming curriculum supporting Python and C++ choices
Student preference correlation with prior programming language familiarity
Performance analysis showing C++ advantages primarily from prior knowledge
Systematic documentation of Python-specific pitfalls in GPU programming
Teaching recommendations for improving Python GPU learning

metrics.secondary: Performance differences between Python and C++

limitations: Small sample size (19 students); limited to computer science curriculum; long-term retention not measured; specific pitfall examples not provided in abstract
primary_theme: GPU Programming Education and Language Accessibility
